originalTitle: Risk Appetite Recovers but French Risks Remain Elevated; AI Earnings Awaited
content:
Risk Sentiment Shows Signs of Improvement

The US dollar traded mixed against its major peers yesterday, losing ground against the euro and the risk-linked Aussie and Kiwi , while gaining ground against the traditional safe-havens Yen and Franc . The greenback finished Monday virtually unchanged against the pound and the loonie .

This trading pattern in the FX sphere suggests an improvement in market appetite. The rebound on Wall Street and the euro ’s recovery despite the unrest in France also support this view. The Aussie and the Kiwi may also have been receiving strong support from China’s better-than-expected GDP data for Q3, released on Monday. China is Australia’s and New Zealand’s main trading ally.

French Politics Remain a Threat for the Euro

Buyers of euro/dollar have repeatedly emerged in the 1.1100-1.1200 area, possibly reflecting technical positioning. In the bigger picture, this territory offered support in May 2025 and acted as resistance in August and September 2024. The euro buying could also suggest that markets are treating France’s developments as a local sovereign-risk problem, rather than the beginning of a systemic euro-area crisis. Indeed, Eurozone money markets are still pointing to 75bps worth of additional ECB rate hikes by the end of 2027.

That said, the French - German 10-year yield spread widened to around 148bps today and European stock bourses are trading in the red, which means that France remains a material downside risk. A failure by Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu to pass a budget through a fragmented parliament, or evidence that stress is spreading to other Eurozone economies’ debt, could further anger euro bears, who may seek to extend the prevailing steep downtrend.

Yen Traders Remain Alert to Intervention Risks

Elsewhere, the yen slipped yesterday, but it seems to be taking advantage of the dollar’s weakness today, entering a recovery mode after dollar/yen hit resistance at around 158.65.

It seems that traders remain concerned about the possibility of intervention by Japanese authorities around the 159-160 zone, as Prime Minister Takaichi warned for the umpteenth time last week that authorities would scrutinize exchange-rate moves and “respond appropriately”.

That said, even if intervention occurs in the weeks or months to come, dollar/yen traders may treat it as a renewed buying opportunity. Although BoJ Governor Ueda signaled lately the need for more rate hikes, the scenario where the Bank meets expectations of 85bps worth of additional rate increases by the end of 2027 appears to be unlikely.

Prime Minister Takaichi has repeatedly called on the BoJ to keep interest rates low. Although she cannot directly influence the Bank’s decisions, she can exert indirect influence through Board appointments. The two members who dissented from the latest rate hike were appointed by her, and she will have the opportunity to appoint more doves to the Board next summer. That’s why the yen may be destined to remain under pressure for a while longer, even if more intervention episodes take place in the foreseeable future.

Tech Rebounds Ahead of Major Earnings

On Wall Street, the Dow Jones closed Monday’s session unchanged, but both the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq eked out gains, with the latter gaining more than 1%. The gains were led by the technology sector, with Amazon (NASDAQ: AMZN ) jumping 5% after Morgan Stanley named it a top pick, while Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA ) and Tesla (NASDAQ: TSLA ) also rose. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index ended an eight-session losing streak, which was its longest since 2008.

Anxiety and concerns about AI borrowing rose after CoreWeave’s (NASDAQ: CRWV ) shares fell around 15% on headlines that it has financed its data center expansion with tens of billions of dollars of debt. However, yesterday’s rebound suggests that investors remain willing to buy AI-related shares after sharp declines.

Focus today shifts to Netflix’s (NASDAQ: NFLX ) earnings results after the closing bell, while tomorrow, it will be the turn of Meta (NASDAQ: META ) and Tesla to report. AI spending and the outlook will be central to investors’ assessment. Lam Research and Texas Instruments could also attract attention, as their earnings may provide signals on chip demand.
chineseTitle: 风险偏好有所恢复，但法国风险依然升高；AI 收益等待
chineseSummary: 该条目暂未抓取到摘要，建议点击原文链接核对完整信息。
chineseContent:
风险情绪出现改善迹象

昨天，美元兑主要货币涨跌互现，兑欧元、风险相关澳元和新西兰元下跌，兑传统避险货币日元和法郎上涨。美元兑英镑和加元周一收盘几乎没有变化。

外汇领域的这种交易模式表明市场胃口有所改善。尽管法国动荡，华尔街的反弹和欧元的复苏也支持了这一观点。周一公布的中国第三季度GDP数据好于预期，澳元和新西兰元也可能得到了强有力的支撑。中国是澳大利亚和新西兰的主要贸易盟友。

法国政治仍然是欧元的威胁

欧元/美元买家在1.1100-1.1200区域反复出现，可能反映了技术定位。从更大的角度来看，该领域在 2025 年 5 月提供了支撑，并在 2024 年 8 月和 9 月提供了阻力。欧元买盘还可能表明，市场将法国的事态发展视为当地主权风险问题，而不是系统性欧元区危机的开始。事实上，欧元区货币市场仍预计欧洲央行到 2027 年底将额外加息 75 个基点。

尽管如此，法国-德国 10 年期国债收益率利差今天扩大至 148 个基点左右，欧洲股市出现亏损，这意味着法国仍然面临重大下行风险。如果总理塞巴斯蒂安·勒科尔努未能在四分五裂的议会中通过预算，或者有证据表明压力正在蔓延到其他欧元区经济体的债务，可能会进一步激怒欧元空头，他们可能会寻求延续当前的急剧下跌趋势。

日元交易者对干预风险保持警惕

其他方面，日元昨天下跌，但今天似乎利用了美元的疲软，在美元/日元触及158.65附近阻力后进入复苏模式。

交易员似乎仍然担心日本当局在 159-160 区间附近进行干预的可能性，因为日本首相高市上周多次警告称，当局将密切关注汇率走势并“做出适当反应”。

也就是说，即使干预在未来几周或几个月内发生，美元/日元交易者也可能将其视为新的买入机会。尽管日本央行行长上田近期表示需要进一步加息，但该行在 2027 年底前额外加息 85 个基点的预期似乎不太可能实现。

日本首相高市多次呼吁日本央行保持低利率。尽管她不能直接影响世行的决策，但她可以通过董事会任命施加间接影响。反对最近加息的两名成员是由她任命的，明年夏天她将有机会任命更多鸽派成员。这就是为什么日元可能注定会在更长一段时间内继续承受压力，即使在可预见的未来会发生更多干预事件。

科技股在主要盈利之前反弹

华尔街方面，道琼斯指数周一收盘持平，但标准普尔 500 指数和纳斯达克指数均微幅上涨，后者涨幅超过 1%。科技股领涨，摩根士丹利将亚马逊 (NASDAQ: AMZN) 列为首选股，股价上涨 5%，而英伟达 (NASDAQ: NVDA) 和特斯拉 (NASDAQ: TSLA) 也上涨。费城半导体指数结束了自 2008 年以来最长的八个交易日连跌。

CoreWeave（纳斯达克股票代码：CRWV）因举债数百亿美元为其数据中心扩张提供资金的头条新闻导致其股价下跌约 15%，之后，人们对人工智能借贷的焦虑和担忧加剧。然而，昨天的反弹表明投资者在大幅下跌后仍然愿意购买人工智能相关股票。

今天的焦点转移到 Netflix（纳斯达克股票代码：NFLX）收盘后的盈利结果，而明天，将轮到 Meta（纳斯达克股票代码：META）和特斯拉发布报告。人工智能支出和前景将成为投资者评估的核心。 Lam Research 和德州仪器 (Texas Instruments) 也可能引起关注，因为它们的收益可能会提供芯片需求的信号。
